questions.question: In a chemical reaction, what name is given to the starting chemicals that undergo a reaction?
options: Catalysts
Reactants
Products
Solutes

questions.question: What do we call the chemicals that are newly formed as a result of a chemical reaction?
options: Reactants
Solvents
Products
Elements

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the atoms in the products of a chemical reaction compared to the reactants?
options: The products contain completely new atoms that were created during the reaction.
The products contain exactly the same atoms as the reactants.
The products contain fewer atoms because some are destroyed.
The products contain more atoms than the reactants.

questions.question: What happens to the bonding of atoms during a chemical reaction when products are formed?
options: The atoms remain bonded in exactly the same way.
The atoms are bonded differently in the products compared to the reactants.
The atoms lose all of their chemical bonds permanently.
The atoms are merged together into a single giant atom.

questions.question: How did John Dalton model an atom in his scientific theory?
options: As a cloud of negative charge containing a positive nucleus
As a sphere that cannot be broken up
As a hollow ring containing smaller particles
As a liquid droplet that can split easily

questions.question: What is a defining feature of a chemical element?
options: It is made up of at least three different types of atoms.
It is made up of only one type of atom.
It can easily be split into other simpler substances by physical means.
It is always a mixture of metals and non-metals.

questions.question: What information do the chemical symbols in a substance's chemical formula provide?
options: The temperature at which the substance melts
The speed of the chemical reaction
Each element (each type of atom) that the substance contains
The state of matter of the substance at room temperature

questions.question: In a chemical formula, what do the small subscript numbers written next to the chemical symbols represent?
options: The charge of each atom
The number of each type of atom in the compound
The number of chemical reactions needed to make it
The physical state of each element

questions.question: Carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO2) both consist of carbon and oxygen. How do they differ?
options: They contain the same elements but in a different ratio.
One is a pure element and the other is a mixture.
They contain different types of carbon atoms.
They have the exact same chemical and physical properties.

questions.question: Which statement best describes metalloid elements?
options: They only have the properties of highly reactive non-metals.
They have some properties of metals and some properties of non-metals.
They are metals that can never conduct electricity.
They are completely inert gases found on the far right of the periodic table.

questions.question: Sodium is a highly reactive metal and chlorine is a toxic gas, but together they form sodium chloride (table salt). What does this demonstrate about compounds?
options: A compound always retains the exact physical properties of its constituent elements.
A compound may have completely different properties to the elements it is made from.
A compound is a simple physical mixture where elements do not bond.
Compounds always have properties that are the average of their elements.

questions.question: Although it is a non-metal, which of the following is an excellent conductor of both electricity and heat?
options: Sulfur
Helium
Graphite
Phosphorus

questions.question: Where are metals and non-metals generally located on the periodic table?
options: Metals are on the right side, non-metals are on the left side and in the middle.
Metals are on the left side and in the middle, non-metals are on the right side.
Metals are only at the top, non-metals are only at the bottom.
Metals and non-metals are randomly scattered with no organized pattern.

questions.question: What is meant by a diatomic molecule, such as oxygen (O2) or nitrogen (N2)?
options: A molecule containing three different elements
A molecule that contains two atoms bonded together
An atom that cannot bond with any other atom
A compound made of a metal and a non-metal

questions.question: When a simple compound is formed between a metal and a non-metal, how does its name typically end?
options: -ate
-ide
-ite
-ic

questions.question: What is the name given to compounds that consist of metal atoms bonded to a -CO3 group?
options: Metal sulfates
Metal nitrates
Metal carbonates
Metal chlorides

questions.question: Which group of compounds is formed when metal atoms are bonded to -SO4?
options: Metal sulfates
Metal nitrates
Metal carbonates
Metal oxides
